title: Definition
body_md: A category $\mathsf{D}$ with an initial object is Nullstellensatzian if every compact, nonterminal object admits a map to the initial object. An object $x$ in a category $\mathsf{C}$ is Nullstellensatzian if the slice category $x/\mathsf{C}$ of $x$-algebras is Nullstellensatzian.

body_md: Let $k$ be a Nullstellensatzian Tambara functor. Then $k$ is isomorphic to the coinduction of an algebraically closed field, i.e., $k$ is the fixed-point Tambara functor associated to the $G$-ring $\operatorname{Fun}(G,F)$ for $F$ algebraically closed.

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of finite $G$-sets. The functor $\Sigma_f : \mathsf{Set}^{G}/X \to \mathsf{Set}^{G}/Y$ defined by $g \mapsto f \circ g$ sits in an adjoint triple
                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            {\mathsf{Set}^{G}/X} \\
            \\
            {\mathsf{Set}^{G}/Y}
            \arrow["{\Sigma_f}"', shift right=5, from=1-1, to=3-1]
            \arrow["{\Pi_f}", shift left=5, from=1-1, to=3-1]
            \arrow["{f^*}"{description}, from=3-1, to=1-1]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    where $f^*$ is given by pullback along $f$, and $\Pi_f$ is the functor defined on objects by
    \[\Pi_f(g : A \to X) := \left\{(y, t) : y \in Y, t \in 
                                      
    \Gamma(g,f^{-1}(y))
    \right\} \xrightarrow{(y,t) \mapsto y} Y,\]
    where for $g: Z\to X$, and $A\subseteq X$, 
    \[
        \Gamma(g,A) := \{t \in \mathsf{Set}(A, Z) \mid g\circ t = 1_A \} 
        = \prod_{a\in A} g^{-1}(a)
    \]
    is the set of sections of $g$ on the subset $A$.
    The $G$-action is given by
    $g(y,t) = (gy, x\mapsto gt(g^{-1}x))$.

\label{def:poly_g part 1}

    \begin{itemize}

        \item morphisms $X \to Y$ are isomorphism classes of \emph{bispans}, i.e. diagrams

              \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&,row sep=tiny]
                      \& A \& B \\

                      \& {A'} \& {B'}
                      \arrow[from=1-2, to=1-3]

                      \arrow[from=3-2, to=2-1]
                      \arrow[from=3-2, to=3-3]

title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn:fixed-pt-tambara-functor}
If $R$ is a commutative ring with $G$ action, then the fixed point
Tambara functor of $R$, $\underline{R}$,
is the $G$-Tambara functor defined by $\underline{R}(G/H)= R^H$,
$c_{H,g} x = gx$, and when $H\subseteq K$, $\operatorname{res}^K_H x = x$, 
\[ \operatorname{tr}_H^K x = \sum_{kH\in K/H} kx
\text{, and }
\operatorname{nm}_H^K x = \prod_{kH\in K/H} kx.
\]

label: lem:fp-tambara-functor-adjt-to-eval-at-underlying
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fp-tambara-functor-adjt-to-eval-at-underlying}
    The fixed-point Tambara functor construction is right adjoint 
    to the evaluation functor $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}:\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}\to \mathsf{CRing}^{G}$ that 
    sends a Tambara functor $T$ to the ring $T(G/e)$ with its 
    Weyl group action.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring with $G$-action and $T$ be a 
    $G$-Tambara functor. We'll describe the unit and counit of the 
    adjunction.

    The unit map,
    $\eta_T:T\to \underline{T(G/e)}$, is given componentwise by the 
    restriction maps
    $\operatorname{res}^H_e : T(G/H)\to T(G/e)^H$. That these maps are compatible 
    with the norms and transfers follows from the rules for composition.
    The counit map is even more straightforward, since $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}(\underline{S})=S^e=S$, and the counit map will just be the identity map.

    The triangle identities follow from the facts that 
    $\eta_{\underline{S}}$ reduces to the identity map $\underline{S}\to \underline{S}$
    and that the $G/e$ component of $\eta_T$ is the identity map 
    $T(G/e)\to T(G/e)$.

title: Lemma
body_md:
If $R$ is a Green functor and $A$ is a commutative ring, then
    the levelwise tensor product $R\otimes A$ represents the 
    functor that sends a Green functor $S$ to pairs $(f,g)$
    of a Green functor morphism $f:R\to S$ and a ring morphism 
    $g:A\to S(*)$. The universal pair consists of 
    the Green functor 
    map $\iota_R : R\to R\otimes A$ which sends $r$ to $r\otimes 1$ and 
    the ring map $\iota_A: A\to R(*)\otimes A$ which sends $a$ to $1\otimes a$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $S$ is a Green functor, then a map $\phi: R\otimes A\to S$
    has ring maps $\phi_X : R(X)\otimes A\to S(X)$ as components.

    The component of our natural transformation 
    corresponding to the pair 
    $(\iota_R,\iota_A)$ is the map
    $\mathsf{Green}_{G}(R\otimes A, S)\to \mathsf{Green}_{G}(R,S)\otimes \mathsf{Ring}(A, S(*))$
    that sends $\phi: R\otimes S$ to the pair 
    $(\phi\iota_R, \phi_*\iota_A)$.

    To show that this is an isomorphism, we'll show that this map 
    is invertible. So suppose we're given $f:R\to S$ and 
    $g:A\to S(*)$. Then if we let $t_X:X\to *$ be the terminal 
    map and $t_X^* : S(*)\to S(X)$ be the restriction, 
    then we can define 
    $\psi_X : R(X)\otimes A \to S(X)$ to be 
    \[ 
    R(X)\otimes A\overset{{f_X\otimes t_X^*g}}{\rightarrow} S(X)\otimes S(X) \to S(X).
    \]

    Then for any map $\alpha:X\to Y$, if $\alpha^*$ is the restriction map 
    along $\alpha$, then 
    \[
    \alpha^* \psi_Y(r\otimes a) = 
    (\alpha^* f_Y(r))(\alpha^*t_Y^*g(a))  
    = (f_X(\alpha^*r))(t_X^* g(a))
    = \psi_X(\alpha^*(r\otimes a)).
    \]
    Similarly, if $T_{\alpha}$ represents the transfer map along 
    $\alpha$, then 
    \[
    T_{\alpha}\psi_X(r\otimes a)
    =T_{\alpha} (f_X(r) t_X^* g(a))
    =T_{\alpha} (f_X(r) \alpha^*t_Y^* g(a))
    = (T_{\alpha} f_X(r)) t_Y^*g(a)
    \]
    \[
    = f_Y(T_{\alpha} r)t_Y^*g(a)
    = \psi_Y(T_{\alpha}(r\otimes a)).
    \]
    So $\psi$ is a valid map of Green functors.

    Then $\psi\iota_R(r) = \psi(r\otimes 1) = f(r)$, and 
    $\psi_*\iota_A(a) = \psi_*(1\otimes a) = g(a)$. 
    Conversely, if we start with a map $\phi$ and build $\psi$
    from $f=\phi\iota_R$ and $g=\phi_*\iota_A$, then 
    \[ 
    \psi_X(r\otimes a) = \of*{\phi_X\iota_R(r)}\of*{t_X^*\phi_*\iota_A(a)}
    = \phi_X(r\otimes 1)\phi_X(1\otimes a)
    = \phi_X(r\otimes a).
    \]

title: Corollary
body_md: There is a natural isomorphism $R\otimes A\cong R\boxtimes (\mathcal{A}\otimes A)$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is the Burnside Tambara functor.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the above corollary, since $\mathcal{A}$ is initial in Green functors,
    so the category of Green functors is equivalent to the 
    category of 
    $\mathcal{A}$-algebras, the adjoint to evaluation at $*$ from Green
    functors is $A\mapsto \mathcal{A} \otimes A$. Then since $\boxtimes$
    is the coproduct of Green functors, $S\mapsto R\boxtimes S$
    is left adjoint to the forgetful functor from $R$-algebras
    to Green functors.

title: Theorem
body_md:
If $M$ is a semi-Mackey functor, thought of as having
    restrictions and norms, then there is a 
    free Tambara functor generated by $M$, $\mathcal{A}[M]$, 
    whose elements over a given $G$-set $X$ are isomorphism classes
    of pairs 
    $(\alpha : S\to X, m\in M(S))$, which can be thought of 
    as formal transfers $T_{\alpha}m$. Here free means that 
    the functor $M\mapsto \mathcal{A}[M]$ is 
    left adjoint to the forgetful functor 
    from Tambara functors to their multiplicative semi-Mackey 
    functors. Moreover, the same is true 
    if you choose a subcategory of allowed norms and work with the 
    corresponding 
    incomplete semi-Mackey functors and incomplete Tambara functors.

name: Nakaoka

title: Lemma
body_md:
If $M$ is an ordinary monoid, and $\underline{M}$ is the 
constant semi-Mackey functor on $M$, then $\mathcal{A}[\underline{M}]$ 
is isomorphic as a Green functor to $\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathbb{Z}[M]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The key is to show that there is a natural isomorphism
$\mathsf{Green}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[\underline{M}],S) \cong \mathsf{Mon}(M, S(*))$. Then 
we have the sequence of natural isomorphisms
\[ 
\mathsf{Green}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[\underline{M}], S)
\cong \mathsf{Mon}(M, S(*))
\cong \mathsf{CRing}(\mathbb{Z}[M], S(*))
\cong \mathsf{Green}_{G}(\mathcal{A}\otimes \mathbb{Z}[M], S),
\]
which shows $\mathcal{A}[\underline{M}]\cong \mathcal{A}\otimes \mathbb{Z}[M]$.

Nakaoka's theorem constructs the same object regardless of 
what subcategory of allowed norms you take, so
if we take the minimal subcategory generated by the fold maps,
then in fact, Nakaoka's theorem tells us 
\[ 
\mathsf{Green}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[\underline{M}],S)\cong \mathsf{Coeff}_{\mathsf{Mon}}(\underline{M}, S)\cong \mathsf{Mon}(M, S(*)),
\]
where $\mathsf{Coeff}_{\mathsf{Mon}}$ is the category 
of coefficient systems in monoids, which is to say product 
preserving functors from $\mathsf{Set}^{G}{}^{\text{op}}$ to $\mathsf{Mon}$.

title: Proposition

\label{prop:free-green-has-norms-and-is-levelwise-tensor}

title: Lemma
body_md:
Given a commutative ring $R$, the right adjoint to the forgetful 
    functor, $U:\mathsf{CRing}^{G} \to \mathsf{CRing}$, sends $R$ to 
    the $G$-ring $\operatorname{Fun}(G,R)$ of 
    functions $G \to R$, whose $G$-action is given by 
    $(g \cdot \varphi)(h) = \varphi(h g)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring with $G$-action, and let $R$ be an 
    ordinary commutative ring. 
    
    If $\varphi : S \to \operatorname{Fun}(G,R)$ is a map of commutative rings 
    with $G$ action, then the adjoint, $\tilde{\varphi}:US\to R$,
    is given by
    $\tilde{\varphi}(s) := \varphi_s(e)$. On the other hand, if we start with
    some ring map
    $\tilde{\varphi}: US\to R$, we can recover $\varphi$ from the fact that
    if $\varphi$ exists, it must satisfy
    \[\varphi_s(g) = \varphi_s(e\cdot g) = (g\cdot \varphi_s)(e) = \varphi_{gs}(e) = \tilde{\varphi}(gs),\]
    but that gives us a definition of $\varphi$.

label: prop:free-forget-kalg
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:free-forget-kalg}
    Let $k$ be a Tambara functor. There is a free-forgetful adjunction between Tambara functors and $k$-algebras. The forgetful functor sends a $k$-algebra $k \rightarrow K$ to $K$, and the free functor is given by the box product $k \boxtimes -$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This comes from the fact that $\boxtimes$ is the coproduct in the category of Tambara functors. Given a Tambara functor $T$ and a $k$-algebra $\alpha : k \to K$, a morphism of $k$-algebras $k \boxtimes T \to K$ is a morphism $f : k \boxtimes T \to K$ of Tambara functors making the diagram
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            T \&\& {k \boxtimes T} \&\& K \\
            \\
            \&\& k
            \arrow["i", from=3-3, to=1-3]
            \arrow["\alpha"', from=3-3, to=1-5]
            \arrow["f", dashed, from=1-3, to=1-5]
            \arrow["j", from=1-1, to=1-3]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    commute, where $i$ and $j$ are the structure maps of the coproduct
    $k \boxtimes T$. By the universal property of coproducts, $f$ is
    uniquely determined by the data of a pair of morphisms
    $(f_1 : k \to K, f_2 : T \to K)$ such that $f_1 \circ i = \alpha$.
    Sending $f$ to $f_2 \circ j$ gives a natural bijection from
    $\mathsf{Alg}_{k}(k \boxtimes T, K)$ to $\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(T,K)$.

    \[ \left( \operatorname{colim}_i K_i \right)(G/H) \cong \operatorname{colim}_i \left( K_i(G/H) \right)\]

label: cor:filtered-colimits-computed-levelwise
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:filtered-colimits-computed-levelwise}
    Let $k$ be a Tambara functor. In the category of $k$-algebras, filtered colimits may be computed levelwise.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{prop:free-forget-kalg}, we have an isomorphism
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{Alg}_{k}(k[x_H], \operatorname{colim} K) & = \mathsf{Alg}_{k}(k \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_H], \operatorname{colim} K) \\
                                 & \cong \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[x_H], \operatorname{colim} K)      \\
                                 & \cong \operatorname{colim}_i \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[x_H], K_i)  \\
                                 & \cong \operatorname{colim}_i \mathsf{Alg}_{k}(k[x_H], K_i)
    \end{align*}
    for filtered diagrams $K : I \to \mathsf{Alg}_{k}$.

title: Definition
body_md: The free polynomial $k$-algebra on $n$ generators in respective levels $H_1,...,H_n$ is \[ k[x_{H_1},...,x_{H_n}] := k \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_{H_1}] \boxtimes ... \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_{H_n}] \]

label: lem:res of free on fixed
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:res of free on fixed}
    For any $G$-Tambara functor $k$, $R^G_H(k[x_G]) \cong (R^G_H k)[x_H]$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We start with the case $k = \mathcal{A}$. Because coinduction is given by precomposition with restriction, we have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{Tamb}_{H}(R^G_H \mathcal{A}[x_G], T) & \cong \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(\mathcal{A}[x_G], C_H^G T) \\
                                  & \cong (C_H^G T)(G/G)            \\
                                  & \cong T(H/H)                    \\
                                  & \cong \mathsf{Tamb}_{H}(\mathcal{A}[x_H], T)
    \end{align*}
    naturally in $T$. Thus, $R^G_H \mathcal{A}[x_G] \cong \mathcal{A}[x_H]$.

    Next, since $R^G_H$ is a left adjoint, it preserves coproducts. Thus,
    \[R^G_H k[x_H] \cong R^G_H (k \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_G]) \cong R^G_H k \boxtimes R^G_H \mathcal{A}[x_G] \cong (R^G_H k)[x_H].\qedhere\]

label: prop:free-at-fixed-pts-is-levelwise-fg
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Lemma
body_md:
If $R$ is a Tambara functor, then for $K\le H$, 
  $\operatorname{res}^H_K : R(G/H)\to R(G/K)$ is an integral map 
  of rings.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the Tambara functor 
  $S:=R[\underline{x}]$, which is isomorphic to the levelwise
  tensor product by \Cref{prop:free-green-has-norms-and-is-levelwise-tensor},
  so we have that $S(G/H)\cong R(G/H)[x]$. 
  
  Then if $a\in R(G/K)$, let $p(x) = \operatorname{nm}_K^H (x-a) 
  \in R(G/H)[x]$. The 
  Mackey double coset formula tells us that $(x-a)$ 
  divides $\operatorname{res}^H_K\operatorname{nm}_K^H (x-a)$, and 
  $p(a) = \operatorname{res}^H_K(p)(a)$, so $p(a)=0$.
  Since $p$ is monic 
  (its leading term is $N_K^H x = x^{[H:K]}$),
  $a$ is integral over $R(G/H)$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We induct on the order of $G$. When $G=e$ is the trivial group, 
  $\mathcal{A}_e[x_e] \cong \mathbb{Z}[x]$, which is certainly finitely generated.
  Otherwise, assume that the 
  result holds for all subgroups of $G$. Note that 
  $R^G_H \mathcal{A}_G[x_G] = \mathcal{A}_H[x_H]$, so this tells us that all 
  of the rings $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$ are finitely 
  generated for $G\ne H$.

  Now for each $H < G$ choose generators $y^H_i$ 
  of $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$, and for later convenience 
  assume that $y^H_0 = \operatorname{res}^G_H x_G$ for each subgroup 
  $H$. For each $y^H_i$, by integrality of restriction maps we can choose a monic polynomial $m^H_i(s) \in \mathcal{A}_G[x_G][s]$
  such that $m^H_i(y^H_i)=0$.

  Let $S$ be the subring 
  of $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/G)$ generated by $\mathcal{A}_G(G/G)$, 
  the coefficients of the $m^H_i$, and the elements 
  $\operatorname{nm}_H^G y^H_i$. This is a finitely generated ring,
  since $\mathcal{A}_G(G/G)$ is finitely generated, and there 
  are only finitely many elements $y^H_i$. 
  Moreover, by construction each of the rings 
  $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$ is still integral over $S$, since 
  $S$ contains the coefficients of monic polynomials 
  killing the generators of those rings. Therefore,
  since the rings $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$ are finitely
  generated and integral over $S$, they are module finite 
  over $S$. So for each proper subgroup $H$ we can choose 
  finitely many elements $z^H_j$ which generate 
  $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$ as a module over $S$.

  Then $S$ and the elements $\operatorname{tr}_H^G z^H_j$ 
  together generate all of $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/G)$.
  This is because $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/G)$ is generated
  over $\mathcal{A}_G(G/G)$ by 
  elements of the form 
  \[\operatorname{tr}_H^G \prod_i \operatorname{nm}_{K_i}^H \operatorname{res}^G_{K_i} x_G,\]
  for some choice of $K_i\le H\le G$. 
  Now if $H=G$, all of the elements 
  $\operatorname{nm}_{K_i}^G\operatorname{res}^G_{K_i} x_G$ are in $S$ already,
  since $\operatorname{res}^G_{K_i}x_G = y^{K_i}_0$ and $S$ includes
  the norms of our chosen generators. 
  
  Otherwise, when $H\ne G$, the generator is of the 
  form $\operatorname{tr}_H^G a$ for some element $a$ of 
  $\mathcal{A}_G[x_G](G/H)$, and we can write $a$ in the form 
  $\sum_{k=1}^n \operatorname{res}^G_H(a_k)z^H_k$ for elements 
  $a_k\in S$.
  But then 
  \[
    \operatorname{tr}_H^G a = \operatorname{tr}_H^G \sum_{k=1}^n a_k\cdot z^H_k
    = \sum_{k=1}^n a_k \operatorname{tr}_H^G z^H_k,
  \]
  which is in our ring.

title: Definition
body_md: An object $x$ in a category $\mathsf{C}$ is said to be \emph{compact} if the functor $\mathsf{C}(x,-)$ preserves filtered colimits.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $k$ be a Tambara functor. A $k$-algebra is finitely generated if it is a quotient of some $k[x_{H_1}, \dots, x_{H_n}]$, and finitely presented if furthermore the quotient is by a finitely generated Nakaoka ideal. Equivalently, a finitely presented $k$-algebra is the coequalizer of a diagram \[ k[x_{H_i}]_{i \in I} \rightrightarrows k[x_{H_j}]_{j \in J}\] with $I$ and $J$ finite sets.
head: environment

label: prop:compact same as fp
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:compact same as fp}
    Let $k$ be a Tambara functor. A $k$-algebra is compact if and only if it is finitely presented.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows immediately from \cite[Corollary 3.13]{Adamek_Rosicky_1994} once we establish that the category of $k$-algebras is a multi-sorted variety. So, we will encode the category of $k$-algebras as the category of algebras for a multi-sorted equational theory.

    We have one sort for each subgroup of $G$, so that a $k$-algebra $X$ consists of sets $\{X(G/H)\}_{H \leq G}$. We have a nullary operation $x : * \to X(G/H)$ for each $x \in k(G/H)$, encoding the structure map $k \to X$. We additionally have unary operations $\operatorname{res}, \operatorname{nm}, \operatorname{tr}, \operatorname{c}$ to encode the Tambara operations of $X$, and nullary, unary, and binary operations at each level of $X$ to encode the commutative ring structures of the levels of $X$. Then we impose equational axioms which encode the axioms of a Tambara functor, as well as the fact that $k \to X$ is a homomorphism of Tambara functors. Algebras for this equational theory are precisely $k$-algebras.

label: lem:left-adjoint-preserves-compacts
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:left-adjoint-preserves-compacts}
    Let $F : \mathsf{C} \to \mathsf{D}$ be left adjoint to some functor $G$ which preserves filtered colimits. Then $F$ sends compact objects to compact objects.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $x$ be a compact object of $\mathsf{C}$, and let $Y : I \to \mathsf{D}$ be a filtered diagram in $\mathsf{D}$. We have
    \begin{align*}
        \mathsf{D}(Fx, \operatorname{colim} Y) & \cong \mathsf{C}(x, G \operatorname{colim} Y)           \\
                                        & \cong \mathsf{C}(x, \operatorname{colim} (G \circ Y))   \\
                                        & \cong \operatorname{colim}_i \mathsf{C}(x, G Y_i)       \\
                                        & \cong \operatorname{colim}_i \mathsf{D}(F x, Y_i),
    \end{align*}
    so $Fx$ is a compact object of $\mathsf{D}$.

label: lem:pres-filt-colims
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first claim is \cite[Corollary 1.4]{osmond_coslices_2021}. The second claim reduces to the first: notice that $f^* : y/\mathsf{C} \to x/\mathsf{C}$ is also given by
    \[y/\mathsf{C} \cong f/(x/\mathsf{C}) \xrightarrow{\operatorname{cod}} x/\mathsf{C}.\qedhere\]

label: lem:colimits-in-under-categories
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:colimits-in-under-categories}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be a category and $x$ an object in $\mathsf{C}$. If $I$ is a category, then the categories of diagrams $\alpha$ of shape $I$
    in $x/\mathsf{C}$ and of diagrams $\alpha_+$ of shape $I_+$ in $\mathsf{C}$ are equivalent, where $\alpha_+(0)=x$ and $I_+$ is $I$ with a freely adjoined initial object $0$. Moreover, for any diagram $\alpha: I\to x/\mathsf{C}$ the inclusion of $I^+$ into $I^+_+$ induces
    an equivalence of categories from cocones on $\alpha_+$ to cocones
    on $\alpha$, where $-^+$ is the operation of freely adjoining a
    terminal object to a category. Therefore $\alpha$ has a colimit
    if and only if $\alpha_+$ does.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the diagram
    \[
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
        \begin{tikzcd}
            \mathsf{Cocones}(\alpha) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & {\mathsf{Cat}(I^+,x/\mathsf{C})} \arrow[d] \arrow[r, hook] & {\mathsf{Cat}(I^+_+,\mathsf{C})} \arrow[d]        \\
            * \arrow[r, "\alpha"]                        & {\mathsf{Cat}(I,x/\mathsf{C})} \arrow[d] \arrow[r, hook]   & {\mathsf{Cat}(I_+,\mathsf{C})} \arrow[d, "\operatorname{ev}_0"] \\
            & * \arrow[r, hook]                             & \mathsf{C}
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    All of the squares are pullback squares. The lower right square being
    a pullback square proves the first claim, and then the fact that
    the upper left square is a pullback square (by definition of the
    category of cocones to $\alpha$)
    and that the upper right is a pullback square
    tell us that the upper rectangle is also a pullback square,
    so the category of cocones to $\alpha$ is equivalent to the category
    of cocones to $\alpha_+$.
head: environment

label: cor:if-g-preserves-filt-colim-then-so-do-slices-of-g
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that we have a diagram
    $\alpha:I\to y/\mathsf{D}$ where $I$ is a filtered category
    and suppose this has a colimit given by an extension
    $\beta:I^+\to y/\mathsf{D}$.
    Then by \Cref{lem:colimits-in-under-categories} above,
    since $\alpha$ has a colimit the corresponding diagram
    $\alpha_+$ has a colimit which will be given by $\beta_+$.
    If $I$ is filtered then
    $I_+$ is also filtered, so $G\circ \beta_+$ gives the colimit of
    $G\circ \alpha_+$ since $G$ preserves filtered colmits.
    And
    $G\circ\beta_+\cong ((y/G)\circ \beta)_+$, so
    $(y/G)\circ \beta$ is the colimit of $(y/G)\circ \alpha$.
    Therefore $y/G$ preserves filtered colimits.

label: lem:left-adjoint-preserves-compact-morphisms
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:left-adjoint-preserves-compact-morphisms}
    Let $F : \mathsf{C} \to \mathsf{D}$ be a functor having a right adjoint $G$
    that preserves filtered colimits.
                                                                                                            
    Then $F$ sends compact morphisms to compact morphisms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f : x \to y$ be a compact morphism in $\mathsf{C}$. The functor $x/F : x/ \mathsf{C} \to Fx / \mathsf{D}$ has a right adjoint given by $\eta^* \circ Fx/G$, where $\eta$ is the unit of the adjunction $F \dashv G$.
    Since $\eta^*$ preserves filtered colimits by \Cref{lem:pres-filt-colims} and since $Fx/G$ preserves filtered colimits by
    \Cref{cor:if-g-preserves-filt-colim-then-so-do-slices-of-g}
    we have that $(x/F) f = Ff$ is a compact object in
    $Fx / \mathsf{D}$, i.e.\ $Ff$ is a compact morphism in $\mathsf{D}$.
head: environment

label: lem:compact-morphisms-closed-under-comp
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:compact-morphisms-closed-under-comp}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ be a category. The class of compact morphisms in $\mathsf{C}$ is closed under composition.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $f : x \to y$ and $g : y \to z$ be compact morphisms in $\mathsf{C}$. Now let $\omega : I \to x/\mathsf{C}$ be a filtered diagram in $x/ \mathsf{C}$, and consider a morphism $\varphi : g \circ f \to \operatorname{colim} \omega$ in $x/\mathsf{C}$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            x \& y \& z \\
            \\
            \&\& \bullet
            \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega}"', curve={height=30pt}, from=1-1, to=3-3]
            \arrow["g", from=1-2, to=1-3]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-3, to=3-3]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    Since $f$ is compact, the morphism $\varphi \circ g : f \to \operatorname{colim} \omega$ factors through $\omega(i_0)$ for some $i_0 \in I$. Let $w_0$ be the codomain of $\omega(i_0)$, so that we have
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            x \& y \& z \\
            \& {w_0} \\
            \&\& \bullet
            \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_0)}"{description}, from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega}"', curve={height=30pt}, from=1-1, to=3-3]
            \arrow["g", from=1-2, to=1-3]
            \arrow["\alpha", color={rgb,255:red,92;green,92;blue,214}, from=1-2, to=2-2]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-3, to=3-3]
            \arrow[from=2-2, to=3-3]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    for some morphism $\alpha$. Now we consider the composition
    \[\omega' := i_0/I \xrightarrow{i_0/\omega} \omega(i_0)/(x/\mathsf{C}) \xrightarrow{\omega(i_0)/\operatorname{cod}} w_0/\mathsf{C} \xrightarrow{\alpha^*} y/\mathsf{C}\]
    which is a filtered diagram in $y/C$. Note that the following diagram commutes:
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            {i_0/I} \& {\omega(i_0)/(x/\mathsf{C})} \& {w_0/\mathsf{C}} \& {y/\mathsf{C}} \\
            I \&\&\& {x/\mathsf{C}}
            \arrow["{i_0/\omega}"', from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\omega'}"{description}, curve={height=-30pt}, from=1-1, to=1-4]
            \arrow["\operatorname{cod}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_0)/\operatorname{cod}}", from=1-2, to=1-3]
            \arrow["\operatorname{cod}"', from=1-2, to=2-4]
            \arrow["{\alpha^*}", from=1-3, to=1-4]
            \arrow["{f^*}", from=1-4, to=2-4]
            \arrow["\omega"', from=2-1, to=2-4]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    Thus, by \Cref{lem:pres-filt-colims} we have
    \[f^* \operatorname{colim} \omega' = \operatorname{colim}(f^* \circ \omega') = \operatorname{colim}(\omega \circ \operatorname{cod}),\]
    and since $I$ is filtered, the image of $\operatorname{cod} : i_0/I \to I$ is a final subcategory of $I$. Overall, this gives
    \[f^* \operatorname{colim} \omega' = \operatorname{colim} \omega,\]
    and in particular we note $\operatorname{cod} \operatorname{colim} \omega' = \operatorname{cod} (f^* \operatorname{colim} \omega') = \operatorname{cod} \operatorname{colim} \omega$.

    So, we have a diagram
                                                                                                                                                             
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            y \& z \\
            \& \bullet
            \arrow["g", from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega'}"', from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-2, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    which we have not yet checked commutes. The commutativity is easy to check, however, because we know that $\operatorname{colim} \omega'$ factors through $\omega'(\operatorname{id}_{i_0})$, i.e. the lower triangle in the commutative square
                                                                                                                                                                                                                     
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            y \& z \\
            {w_0} \& \bullet
            \arrow["g", from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_0)}"', from=1-1, to=2-1]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega'}"{description}, from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-2, to=2-2]
            \arrow[from=2-1, to=2-2]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    commutes. Now, since $g$ is a compact morphism in $\mathsf{C}$, we know that $\varphi$ factors through $\omega'(\gamma)$ for some $\gamma \in i_0/I$. We have $\gamma : i_0 \to i_1$ for some $i_1 \in I$; letting $w_1$ denote the codomain of $\omega(i_1)$, we get
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            x \& y \&\&\& y \&\& z \\
            \& {w_0} \&\&\&\& {w_1} \\
            \& {w_1} \&\&\&\&\& \bullet
            \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-2]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_0)}"{description}, from=1-1, to=2-2]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_1)}"{description}, curve={height=12pt}, from=1-1, to=3-2]
            \arrow["\alpha", from=1-2, to=2-2]
            \arrow["{\omega'(\gamma)}", curve={height=-30pt}, from=1-2, to=3-2]
            \arrow["g", from=1-5, to=1-7]
            \arrow["{\omega'(\gamma)}"{description}, from=1-5, to=2-6]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega'}"', curve={height=30pt}, from=1-5, to=3-7]
            \arrow["\beta"', color={rgb,255:red,92;green,92;blue,214}, from=1-7, to=2-6]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-7, to=3-7]
            \arrow["{\omega(\gamma)}"{description}, from=2-2, to=3-2]
            \arrow[from=2-6, to=3-7]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    for some morphism $\beta$. Putting these diagrams together, we have
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
    \[\begin{tikzcd}[ampersand replacement=\&]
            x \&\& y \&\& z \\
            \&\&\& {w_1} \\
            \&\&\&\& \bullet
            \arrow["f", from=1-1, to=1-3]
            \arrow["{\omega(i_1)}"', from=1-1, to=2-4]
            \arrow["{\operatorname{colim} \omega' \circ f}"', curve={height=24pt}, from=1-1, to=3-5]
            \arrow["g", from=1-3, to=1-5]
            \arrow["{\omega'(\gamma)}"{description}, from=1-3, to=2-4]
            \arrow["\beta"', from=1-5, to=2-4]
            \arrow["\varphi", from=1-5, to=3-5]
            \arrow[from=2-4, to=3-5]
        \end{tikzcd}\]
    and we recall $\operatorname{colim} \omega' \circ f = f^* \operatorname{colim} \omega' = \operatorname{colim} \omega$. Thus, $\beta$ factors $\varphi$ through $\omega(i_1)$. Since $\varphi$ was arbitrary, we conclude that $g \circ f$ is a compact morphism in $\mathsf{C}$, as desired.

label: prop:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-left-reflects-terminal-objects
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-left-reflects-terminal-objects}

    Let $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{D}$ be categories with terminal objects
    and let $F:\mathsf{C}\to \mathsf{D}$ be left adjoint to a functor
    $G:\mathsf{D}\to \mathsf{C}$ that preserves
    filtered colimits. Let $x$ be a Nullstellensatzian object in $\mathsf{D}$. Suppose that:

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $Gx$ is nonterminal.
        \item Precomposition with the
              counit $\epsilon_x^*:x/\mathsf{D}\to FGx/\mathsf{D}$
              has a left adjoint $\epsilon_{x*}$.
        \item The composite
              $\epsilon_{x*}\circ (Gx/F): Gx/\mathsf{C}\to x/\mathsf{D}$
              reflects terminal objects
              (at least when restricted to compact objects).
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $Gx$ is also Nullstellensatzian.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$x$ is Nullstellensatzian by definition
    if and only if $x$ is nonterminal and
    $(x/\mathsf{D})$ is Nullstellensatzian,

    So since $Gx$ is assumed to be nonterminal,
    this follows from applying the previous theorem
    to the composite adjunction
    \[
        Gx/\mathsf{C} \rightleftharpoons FGx/\mathsf{D}
        \rightleftharpoons x/\mathsf{D}.
    \]
    The left adjoint in the first adjunction is given
    by $Gx/F$ with right adjoint $\eta_{Gx}^*\circ (FGx/G)$.
    In the second adjunction the right adjoint
    is $\epsilon_x^*$ and the left adjoint is
    $\epsilon_{x*}$.

    The composite left adjoint reflects terminal objects by assumption,
    so we just need to check that the composite
    right adjoint preserves filtered colimits and
    sends the initial object to the
    initial object. By the triangle identity, the composite right adjoint
    is given by $x/G$ which preserves
    filtered colimits by \Cref{cor:if-g-preserves-filt-colim-then-so-do-slices-of-g}
    and sends $1_x$ to $1_{Gx}$
    as required.

label: cor:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-pushout-cond
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-pushout-cond}
    Let $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{D}$ be categories with terminal objects
    and let $F:\mathsf{C}\to \mathsf{D}$ be left adjoint to a functor
    $G:\mathsf{D}\to \mathsf{C}$ that preserves
    filtered colimits. Let $x$ be a Nullstellensatzian object in $\mathsf{D}$. Assume that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $G$ reflects terminal objects,
        \item $\mathsf{D}$ has all pushouts.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $Gx$ will be Nullstellensatzian if the following
    condition holds:

    For all compact morphisms $\alpha:Gx\to y$ if we form the pushout square
    \[
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
        \begin{tikzcd}
            FGx \arrow[d, "F\alpha"'] \arrow[r, "\epsilon_x"] & x \arrow[d] \\
            Fy \arrow[r]                                      & z
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    and $z$ is terminal in $\mathsf{D}$ then $y$ is terminal in $\mathsf{C}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $x$ is Nullstellensatzian, then it is nonterminal and since
    $G$ reflects terminal objects $Gx$ is nonterminal. So condition 1
    of the proposition holds. Also when $\mathsf{D}$ has pushouts, then
    for any $f:a\to b$ in $\mathsf{D}$, $f^*:b/\mathsf{D}\to a/\mathsf{D}$ has a left
    adjoint, which is given by pushout along $f$. Therefore
    $\epsilon_{x*}$ is given by pushout along $\epsilon_x$.
    So condition 2 holds. That then
    makes the pushout condition above a restatement of condition 3 of
    the proposition.
head: environment

label: prop:ring-of-funs-from-group-is-ac
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:ring-of-funs-from-group-is-ac}
    For a finite group $G$, the
    functor $\operatorname{Fun}(G,-):\mathsf{CRing}\to \mathsf{CRing}^{G}$ preserves Nullstellensatzian
    objects.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$\operatorname{Fun}(G,-)$ is right adjoint to the forgetful functor, and
    if $\operatorname{Fun}(G,A)=0$, then $A=0$, so it reflects terminal objects.
    Moreover, $\mathsf{CRing}^{G}$ and $\mathsf{CRing}$ both have all filtered colimits
    which are computed in $\mathsf{Set}$, and since $G$ is finite,
    $\operatorname{Fun}(G,-)$ commutes with filtered colimits in $\mathsf{Set}$ and therefore
    commutes with filtered colimits of commutative rings as well.

    Therefore we are in the situation of
    \Cref{cor:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-pushout-cond},
    so we just need to check the pushout condition.
    If $k$ is a commutative ring, then the counit $\epsilon_k$
    is evaluation at the identity element of $G$,
    $\operatorname{ev}_e:\operatorname{Fun}(G,k)\to k$.

    If $A$ is an algebra over $\operatorname{Fun}(G,k)$ in $\mathsf{CRing}^{G}$, via a map
    $\alpha: \operatorname{Fun}(G,k)\to A$, then
    the idempotents $\delta_g \in \operatorname{Fun}(G,k)$ which are the
    indicator functions for each of the elements $g\in G$ induce a product
    decomposition
    \[ A=\prod_{g\in G} A\delta_g, \]
    and since $G$ acts transitively on the $\delta_g$, we have that 
    if $A_0 = A\delta_e$, then $A\cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,A_0)$.
    Moreover if we let $\alpha_0$ be the map
    $k\cong k\delta_e\to A\delta_e \cong A_0$,
    then $\alpha\cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,\alpha_0)$.

    Then the pushout square we get is
    \[
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
        \begin{tikzcd}
            {\operatorname{Fun}(G,k)} \arrow[d, "{\operatorname{Fun}(G,\alpha_0)}"'] \arrow[r, "\epsilon_k"] & k \arrow[d, "\alpha_0"] \\
            {\operatorname{Fun}(G,A_0)} \arrow[r, "\epsilon_{A_0}"]                            & A_0
        \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    and if $A_0$ is $0$, then so was $A$.
head: environment

label: lem:fixed-pts-preserves-nullstellensatzian
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:fixed-pts-preserves-nullstellensatzian}
  The fixed point Tambara functor 
  $\underline{-} : \mathsf{CRing}^{G}\to \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$ preserves Nullstellensatzian
  objects.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring with $G$-action.
  Since fixed points are finite limits they commute 
  with filtered colimits and arbitrary limits, 
  and we know that the fixed point Tambara functor 
  is right adjoint to $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}$, and if 
  $\underline{S}=0$, then $S$ must have been zero 
  in the first place. So we just need to check the 
  pushout condition.

  If $A$ is an $\underline{S}$-algebra, then the pushout 
  is $A(G/e)\otimes_{\underline{S}(G/e)} S \cong A(G/e)$.
  So if the pushout is zero, then $A(G/e)$ is zero, 
  which implies that $A$ is zero.

label: lem:eval-has-left-adjt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:eval-has-left-adjt}
    For a finite $G$-set $X$, the functor $\operatorname{ev}_X:\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}\to \mathsf{CRing}$
    has a left adjoint. The same is also true for
    $\operatorname{ev}_{G/H}: \mathsf{Tamb}_{G} \to \mathsf{CRing}^{W_G(H)}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. We can (functorially) write $A$ as a coequalizer of
    free commutative rings,
    $\operatorname{coeq} \mathbb{Z}[x_j:j\in J]\rightrightarrows \mathbb{Z}[x_i:i\in I]$
    for some indexing sets $I$ and $J$ and maps of commutative rings.
    Then we can construct the exact same diagram in Tambara functors
    by adjoining the variables at level $X$ and define
    \[LA = \operatorname{coeq} \mathcal{A}_G[x_j^X:j\in J]\rightrightarrows \mathcal{A}_G[x_i^X:i\in I].\]
    Then for any Tambara functor $S$, we have that $\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(LA,S)$
    is naturally isomorphic to maps $I\to S(X)$ picking out families of
    elements of $S(X)$ that satisfy the relations imposed by the
    coequalizer. And that is naturally isomorphic to $\mathsf{CRing}(A, S(X))$.
    Therefore a left adjoint exists.

    The same proof works when we remember the Weyl action.
head: environment

label: prop:ev-at-underlying-preserves-nullstellensatzian
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the lemma above $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}$ preserves filtered 
  colimits and has a left adjoint. It also reflects 
  terminal objects, because if $k(G/e)=0$, then 
  $1_G = \operatorname{nm}_e^G 1_e =0$, so $k=0$. So we just need 
  to verify the pushout condition.

  Let $L_e$ be the left adjoint to $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}$ 
  constructed above. Then if $A$ is a $k(G/e)$ algebra,
  let $B:= L_e A \boxtimes_{L_e k(G/e)} k$ denote
  the pushout. We want to show that if $B$ is zero, 
  then $A$ must have already been zero. Now recall that 
  $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}$ is also a left adjoint whose right adjoint 
  is the fixed point
  Tambara functor construction. 
  So $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e} B = (\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}L_e A)
  \boxtimes_{\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}L_e k(G/e)} k(G/e)$.
  However, if $S$ is any commutative ring with a $G$-action,
  $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}L_e S \cong S$, since for any other 
  commutative ring with $G$-action, $T$, we have 
  the following natural isomorphisms 
  \[
    \mathsf{CRing}^{G}(\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}L_e S, T)
    \cong 
    \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(L_e S, \underline{T})
    \cong
    \mathsf{CRing}^{G}(S, \operatorname{ev}_{G/e}\underline{T})
    =
    \mathsf{CRing}^{G}(S, T),
  \]
  since $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e}\underline{T} = T^{e} = T$ 
  by definition.

  Therefore 
  $\operatorname{ev}_{G/e} B \cong A\boxtimes_{k(G/e)} k(G/e)\cong A$.
  So if $B$ is zero, $A$ is also zero.

label: cor:constant-Z-is-fp
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:constant-Z-is-fp}
    $\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$ is a compact object in $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
$\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$ is generated as a $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$-algebra (indeed, even as a Tambara functor) by the element $x$ at level $G/G$. Thus, we have a surjection $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}[x_G] \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$.

    Next, we note that $\mathcal{A} \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ is surjective, so \[\mathcal{A}[x_G] = \mathcal{A} \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_G] \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}} \boxtimes \mathcal{A}[x_G] = \underline{\mathbb{Z}}[x_G]\] is surjective. Since $\mathcal{A}[x_G]$ is levelwise finitely generated, we conclude that $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}[x_G]$ is also levelwise finitely generated (in particular, levelwise Noetherian). Thus, every ideal of $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}[x_G]$ is finitely generated. In particular, the kernel of $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}[x_G] \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$ is finitely generated, so $\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$ is compact in $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $S \mapsto \underline{S} : \mathsf{CRing} \to \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$ preserves finite coproducts.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: For the empty coproduct we have directly that $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ is initial in $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$. \cite[Lemma 5.1]{LRZ-etale} shows that $\underline{S \otimes S'} \cong \underline{S} \boxtimes \underline{S'}$, and we must show that this agrees with $\underline{S} \boxtimes_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}} \underline{S'}$. This is simply because $\underline{S} \boxtimes_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}} \underline{S'}$ is defined as a coequalizer of two morphisms which are already equal---morphisms from $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ are unique whenever they exist, because such a morphism consists levelwise of ring homomorphisms from $\mathbb{Z}$.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: $\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}$ has the structure of a co-(commutative ring) object in the category of $\underline{\mathbb{Z}}$-algebras, coming from its co-(commutative ring) object structure in $\mathsf{CRing}$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: $S \mapsto \underline{S} : \mathsf{CRing} \to \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$ is left adjoint to $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}, {-})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Given a morphism $\varphi : \underline{S} \to T$, define a morphism $\widetilde{\varphi} : S \to \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]},T)$ by
    \[\widetilde{\varphi}(s)_{G/H}(f) = f(\varphi_{G/H}(s)).\]
    It is easy to check that $\widetilde{\varphi}(s)$ is a homomorphism of Tambara functors for all $s$, and then that $\widetilde{\varphi}$ is a ring homomorphism. Thus, we obtain a function
    \[\varphi \mapsto \widetilde{\varphi} : \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}(\underline{S},T) \to \mathsf{CRing}(S, \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]}, T))\]
    which is clearly natural in $S$ and $T$. In the other direction, let $\psi : S \to \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]},T)$ be a ring homomorphism. Then define $\widehat\psi : \underline{S} \to T$ by
    \[\widehat\psi_{G/H}(s) = \psi(s)_{G/H}(x).\]
    We check that
    \[\widehat{\widetilde{\varphi}}_{G/H}(s) = \widetilde{\varphi}(s)_{G/H}(x) = \varphi_{G/H}(s)\]
    and
    \[\widetilde{\widehat{\psi}}(s)_{G/H}(x) = \widehat{\psi}_{G/H}(s) = \psi(s)_{G/H}(x),\]
    so these constructions are mutually inverse.

title: Corollary
body_md: $S \mapsto \underline{S} : \mathsf{CRing} \to \mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$ preserves compact morphisms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By \Cref{cor:constant-Z-is-fp}, $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}(\underline{\mathbb{Z}[x]},{-})$ preserves filtered colimits. By \Cref{lem:left-adjoint-preserves-compact-morphisms}, we are done.

label: thm:constant-preserves-compacts
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:constant-preserves-compacts}
    $S \mapsto \underline{S} : \mathsf{CRing} \to \mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$ preserves compact objects and compact morphisms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Because $A/\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}} \cong \mathsf{Alg}_{A} = A/\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$, a morphism in $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$ is compact if and only if it is compact in $\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$. Next, consider a compact object $R \in \mathsf{CRing}$. Then (equivalently) $\mathbb{Z} \to R$ is compact in $\mathsf{CRing}$, so $\underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{R}$ is compact in $\mathsf{Alg}_{\underline{\mathbb{Z}}}$, so $\underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{R}$ is compact in $\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$. Since $\mathcal{A} \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}}$ is also compact (it is surjective), we conclude that $\mathcal{A} \to \underline{R}$ is compact, i.e., $\underline{R}$ is compact in $\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}$.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md: A Tambara functor $k$ is Nullstellensatzian if every compact, nonterminal object in the slice category of Tambara functor algebras over $k$ admits a map to the initial $k$-algebra $\operatorname{id}_k : k \rightarrow k$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: Let $k$ be a Nullstellensatzian Tambara functor. Then $k$ is field-like.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $H \leq G$ and $x \in k(G/H)$ be arbitrary. If $(x)\ne k$, then 
    $q:k\to k/(x)$ is a nonzero, compact $k$-algebra, so it admits a retraction $r:k/(x)\to k$ such that $r\circ q = 1_k$. 
    Then $r(q(x)) = 0 = x$, so $x=0$. So $k$ has no proper nonzero ideals.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: Let $k$ be a Nullstellensatzian Tambara functor. Then $k(G/G)$ is a field.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This is true of any field-like Tambara functor, see \cite[Remark 4.36]{Nak11a}.

label: exl:constant-C-is-not-ac
title: Example
body_md:
\label{exl:constant-C-is-not-ac}
    If $G$ is not the trivial group, the constant Tambara functor at the algebraically closed field $\mathbb{C}$ is not a Nullstellensatzian Tambara functor.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the complex representation $\mathbb{C}[G]$ of $G$, which contains a copy of $\mathbb{C}$ in its fixed points via $1 \mapsto \sum_{g \in G} g$. Let $X := \mathbb{C}[G]/\mathbb{C}$, which is again a complex representation of $G$. Now $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb{C}}(X)$ is a $G$-$\mathbb{C}$-algebra, and we can invert the elements of $G$ to obtain $Y := \operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb{C}}(X)[g^{-1} : g \in G]$, which is again a $G$-$\mathbb{C}$-algebra.

    Since $G$ is not the trivial group, pick a function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $\sum_{g \in G} f(g) = 0$ and $f(g) \neq 0$ for all $g \in G$. This yields a $\mathbb{C}$-linear function $X \to \mathbb{C}$, which then gives us a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra map $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb{C}}(X) \to \operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathbb{C}) \cong \mathbb{C}$. Since $f$ was nowhere-zero, this descends to a $\mathbb{C}$-algebra map $Y \to \mathbb{C}$, and thus we conclude that $Y \neq 0$.

    Now let $E := \underline{Y}$, which is a $\underline{\mathbb{C}}$-algebra. Since $Y$ is finitely presented, it is compact over $\mathbb{C}$, so (by \Cref{thm:constant-preserves-compacts}) $E$ is compact over $\underline{\mathbb{C}}$. Moreover, since $Y \neq 0$ we have $E \neq 0$. Now suppose towards a contradiction that there exists a morphism of Tambara functors $\varphi : E \to \underline{\mathbb{C}}$. In $E(G/e)$ we have $R_e^G T_e^G(e) = \sum_{g \in G} g = 0$, so we get
    \[\lvert G \rvert \varphi(e) = R_e^G T_e^G \varphi(e) = \varphi(R_e^G T_e^G e) = \varphi(0) = 0,\]
    whence $\varphi(e) = 0$. However, $e$ is a unit in $E(G/e) = Y$, so $\varphi(e)$ must be a unit, which is a contradiction.

title: Proof
body_md:
The components of the counit map $k\to \underline{k(G/e)}$,
    are the restriction maps 
    $\operatorname{res}^H_E:k(G/H)\to k(G/e)^H$. Since $k$ is a Tambara field
    these are injective, so we just need 
    to show that the restriction maps are also surjective
    to the fixed points. 

    Let $y\in k(G/e)^H$, and consider the $k$-algebra
    $k[x_{G/H}]/(\operatorname{res}^H_e x_{G/H} -y)$. This is nonzero, since it admits 
    a map to $\underline{k(G/e)}$ sending $x_{G/H}$ to $y$, and it is
    finitely presented, so it admits a retraction, $q$, to $k$.
    Then $\operatorname{res}^H_e q(x_{G/H}) = q(y) = y$ is a lift of $y$ to 
    $k(G/H)$.

label: prop:top-level-is-alg-closed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:top-level-is-alg-closed}
    The functor $\operatorname{ev}_*:\mathsf{Tamb}_{G}\to \mathsf{CRing}$ preserves Nullstellensatzian objects.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since filtered colimits are pointwise in Tambara functors,
    $\operatorname{ev}_{*}$ preserves filtered colimits. By \Cref{lem:eval-has-left-adjt}, $\operatorname{ev}_{*}$ is a right adjoint. If $\operatorname{ev}_*k=0$, then $k=0$, since for any subgroup $H$,
    $1_H\in k(G/H)$ is the restriction of $1_G\in k(G/G)=k(*)$, so
    if $1_G=0$, $1_H=0$ for all $H$, so $k=0$. Therefore $\operatorname{ev}_*$ reflects
    terminal objects.

    Thus we just need to check that when
    $\operatorname{ev}_{*}k\ne 0$ the pushout condition of \Cref{cor:right-adjoints-preserve-AC-if-pushout-cond} holds. Let $L_*$ be the left 
  adjoint to $\operatorname{ev}_*$. Then we need to show 
  that for a finitely presented $k(*)$ 
  algebra, $A$, if the pushout 
  $(L_*A)\boxtimes_{L_*k(*)}k$ is zero, 
  then $A$ must have been zero. Since $A$ is finitely 
  presented, we can write it as a polynomial algebra,
  $A
  \cong 
  k(*)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$,
  for some polynomials $f_1,\ldots, f_m$.
  Then we have that $L_*A \cong 
  L_*k(*)[x_{*,1},\ldots, x_{*,n}]/
  (f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, and the pushout is
  \[ (L_*A)\boxtimes_{L_*k(*)}k
  \cong 
  k[x_{*,1},\ldots,x_{*,n}]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m),\]
  where the $f_i$ are viewed as polynomials 
  in the $x_{*,1},\ldots,x_{*,n}$.

  Consider the Tambara functor
  $k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]$,
  which is isomorphic to the levelwise 
  tensor product of $k$ with $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$
  by \Cref{prop:free-green-has-norms-and-is-levelwise-tensor}. 
  Then we have a map 
  $k[x_{*,1},\ldots,x_{*,n}]
  \to k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]$
  given by sending $x_{*,i}$ to $\underline{x}_i$,
  so by taking quotients we can define a map from 
  the pushout, $k[x_{*,1},\ldots,x_{*,n}]/
  (f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, to 
  $k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]/
  (f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Then we can complete the proof by showing that 
  $\operatorname{ev}_*(k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]/
  (f_1,\ldots,f_m)) \cong A$, since then if the pushout is zero,
  $k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]$ is zero, and therefore 
  $A$ is zero.

  To show this, let $I$ be the ideal of 
  $k(*)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ generated by 
  the polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_m$
  and let $J$ be the ideal of 
  $k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]$
  generated by $f_1,\ldots,f_m$. 
  Certainly we have that $I\subseteq J(*)$,
  and we can complete the proof by showing 
  that this is actually an equality.

  Any element of $J(*)$ can be written
  as a sum of elements  
  of the form 
  \[
    \operatorname{tr}_H^G \of*{
      a \cdot
      \operatorname{nm}_K^H \operatorname{res}^G_K b
    },
  \]
  for subgroups $K\subseteq H\subseteq G$, 
  $a\in 
  \of*{
    k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]
  }(G/H)$
  and $b\in I$.
  so it suffices to show that these generators
  are all contained in $I$. 
  The key here is to show that 
  $\operatorname{nm}_K^H \operatorname{res}^G_K b = \operatorname{res}^G_H b^{[H:K]}$,
  since then 
  \[
    \operatorname{tr}_H^G \of*{
      a \cdot
      \operatorname{nm}_K^H \operatorname{res}^G_K b
    }
    = 
    \operatorname{tr}_H^G \of*{
      a \cdot
      \operatorname{res}^G_H b^{[H:K]}
    }
    = b^{[H:K]}\operatorname{tr}_H^G a \in I.
  \] 

  Then since $k$ is a Tambara field, 
  it satisfies the monomorphic restriction 
  condition, so 
  $k[\underline{x}_1,\ldots,\underline{x}_n]$
  also satisfies the monomorphic restriction 
  condition, since at level $G/H$ it is 
  isomorphic to $k(G/H)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$.

  Therefore we can verify our identity 
  by applying $\operatorname{res}^H_e$ to both sides,
  which gives us
  \[
    \operatorname{res}^H_e \operatorname{res}^G_H b^{[H:K]}
    =
    \prod_{hK \in H/K} (hK)\operatorname{res}^K_e \operatorname{res}^G_K b
    = \operatorname{res}^H_e \operatorname{nm}_K^H\operatorname{res}^G_K b.
    \qedhere
  \]

label: theorem:alg-closed-iff-coinduced
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem:alg-closed-iff-coinduced}
    A Tambara functor $k$ is Nullstellensatzian if and only if $k \cong C_e^G(\mathbb{F})$ for some algebraically closed field $\mathbb{F}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The reverse direction is \cref{cor:coind-preserves-ac}. For the forwards direction, we begin by constructing a useful compact $k$-algebra. Let $K$ be the quotient of $k[x_{G/e}]$ by the following relations at level $G/e$ (recalling $k[x_{G/e}](G/e) \cong k(G/e)[x_g | g \in G]$ from \Cref{prop:underlying-of-free-on-underlying}):
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item (idempotence) $x_g^2 = x_g$
        \item (orthogonality) $x_g x_h = 0$ when $g \neq h$
        \item (completeness) $\displaystyle \sum_{g \in G} x_g = 1$
    \end{enumerate}
    To see that $K$ is nonzero, observe that we may construct a $k$-algebra map $K \rightarrow C_e^G k(G/e)$ as follows. First, choose $k[x_{G/e}] \rightarrow C_e^G k(G/e)$ classifying the choice of any idempotent which determines a projection $C_e^G k(G/e) \cong \operatorname{Fun}(G/e,k(G/e)) \rightarrow k(G/e)$. Next, observe that this map respects the three relations above, so that it descends to $K \rightarrow C_e^G k(G/e)$. Since the codomain of this morphism is nonzero (here we use the assumption that $k$ is nonzero), the domain is also nonzero.

    Since $K$ is a quotient of a finitely generated polynomial algebra by finitely many relations, $K$ is a compact $k$-algebra, and hence admits a section $K \rightarrow k$. Let $y_g \in k(G/e)$ denote the image of $x_g \in K(G/e)$. Then the collection of $y_g$ form a complete set of orthogonal idempotents in $k(G/e)$, hence determine an isomorphism $k(G/e) \cong \prod_{g \in G} k(G/e) \cdot y_g$. Since the 
    $y_g$ form a $G$-orbit, the rings $k(G/e)\cdot y_g$ are all 
    isomorphic, so if we let $A=k(G/e)\cdot y_e$, we can rewrite this 
    as an isomorphism 
    $k(G/e)\cong \operatorname{Fun}(G, A)$.

    Now by \Cref{lem:nullstellensatzian-are-fixed-pt-tam-funcs}
    $k\cong \underline{k(G/e)}$,
    so $k\cong \underline{\operatorname{Fun}(G,A)}$, and we know that 
    $C_e^GA \cong \underline{\operatorname{Fun}(G,A)}$, so this shows that 
    $k$ is coinduced. All that remains is to show that 
    $A$ is an algebraically closed field. 

    However, the diagonal map $\Delta: A\to \operatorname{Fun}(G,A)^G$ is an 
    isomorphism to the $G$-fixed points, so we have that 
    $k(*)\cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,A)^G \cong A$, and $k(*)$ is an algebraically 
    closed field by \cref{prop:top-level-is-alg-closed}.

label: prop:coinduction-and-modules
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:coinduction-and-modules}
    Let $R$ be a ring. Coinduction induces an adjoint equivalence between the category of $R$-modules and the category of $C_e^G R$-modules (defined as Mackey functor modules over the underlying Green functor of $C_e^G R$).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that any Tambara functor has the structure of a monoid with
    respect to the box product, and a module over a Tambara functor is a
    module over the underlying monoid. If $k$ is any $G$-Green functor and
    $M$ is a $k$-module, it follows that every abelian group $M(G/H)$ is a
    $k(G/H)$-module. If $k = C_e^G R$, then we may view $M(G/H)$ as an
    $R$-module through the restriction (i.e., the diagonal action).
    Note that the idempotents in $\operatorname{Fun}(G/H,R)$ determine an $R$-module
    decomposition \[ M(G/H) \cong \operatorname{Fun}(G/H,M_H) \] for some
    $R$-module $M_H$.

    The canonical map \[ M \rightarrow \underline{M(G/e)} \] of Mackey
    functors is surjective in every level by the double coset formula.
    Thus it suffices to show that all restriction maps for $M$ are
    injective. To see this, recall the Frobenius reciprocity relations
    \[ T_f(x) \cdot m = T_f(x \cdot R_f(m)) \] for every
    $f : G/e \rightarrow G/H$. In $C_e^G R$, the unit of each ring
    $C_e^G R(G/H)$ is in the image of the transfer.
    Choosing a preimage of the unit, $x$, we see that if
    $R_f(m) = 0$, then
    \[ m = T_f(x) \cdot m = T_f(x \cdot R_f(m)) = T_f(0) = 0 \]
    hence $R_f$ is injective, as desired.

label: lem:coind-equiv-is-sym-mon
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:coind-equiv-is-sym-mon}
    The equivalence of \cref{prop:coinduction-and-modules} is strong symmetric monoidal (with respect to the tensor product over $\mathbb{F}$ and the box product relative to $C_e^G \mathbb{F}$).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Let $C_e^G X$ and $C_e^G Y$ denote two arbitrary $C_e^G \mathbb{F}$-modules. Since their box product over $C_e^G \mathbb{F}$ is again a module, it is coinduced from a $\mathbb{F}$-module $Z$. Using the natural isomorphism \[ \operatorname{Fun}(G,Z) \cong \left( C_e^G X \boxtimes_{C_e^G \mathbb{F}} C_e^G Y \right)(G/e) \cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,X) \otimes_{\operatorname{Fun}(G,\mathbb{F})} \operatorname{Fun}(G,Y) \] we deduce a natural isomorphism $Z \cong X \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} Y$. Applying coinduction we obtain the desired natural isomorphism \[ C_e^G X \boxtimes_{C_e^G \mathbb{F}} C_e^G Y \cong C_e^G Z \cong C_e^G \left( X \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} Y \right) \textrm{.}\qedhere\]

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $k$ be an $H$-Tambara functor. Then there is a symmetric monoidal equivalence 
    \[ \mathsf{Mod}_{k} \simeq \mathsf{Mod}_{C_H^G k} \] 
    of categories with respect to the relative box product, and an 
    equivalence of categories 
    \[ \mathsf{Alg}_{k} \simeq  \mathsf{Alg}_{C_H^G k} \] of algebras.

title: Corollary
body_md: If $\mathbb{F}$ is algebraically closed, then $C_e^G \mathbb{F}$ is Nullstellensatzian.

title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:K-theory-equiv}
    If $k \cong C_e^G \mathbb{F}$ is Nullstellensatzian, then the equivalence of \cref{prop:coinduction-and-modules} induces an equivalence of $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-ring spectra $K(k) \cong k(\mathbb{F})$.

title: Theorem
body_md: A $G$-ring $k$ is Nullstellensatzian if and only if it is the coinduction of an algebraically closed field $\mathbb{F}$, $k \cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,\mathbb{F})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \Cref{prop:ring-of-funs-from-group-is-ac}, every $G$-ring of the 
    form $\operatorname{Fun}(G,\mathbb{F})$ for $\mathbb{F}$ an algebraically closed 
    field is Nullstellensatzian. 
    For the converse, if a $G$-ring $k$ is 
    Nullstellensatzian, then
    \Cref{lem:fixed-pts-preserves-nullstellensatzian} tells us that 
    $\underline{k}$ is Nullstellensatzian. Therefore 
    $\underline{k}\cong C_e^G(\mathbb{F})$ for some algebraically 
    closed field $\mathbb{F}$ by \Cref{theorem:alg-closed-iff-coinduced}, and evaluating at $G/e$ on both sides 
    gives that $k\cong \operatorname{Fun}(G,\mathbb{F})$.
head: environment

label: theorem:characterization-of-algebraic-closure
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem:characterization-of-algebraic-closure}
    Assume $k$ is field-like. There is a map $k \rightarrow C_e^G \left( \overline{k(G/e)^G} \right)$, where the codomain is the coinduction of an algebraic closure of the field $k(G/e)^G$, and any map from $k$ to a Nullstellensatzian Tambara functor $K$ factors (noncanonically) through this map.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a choice of algebraic closure $k(G/e)^G \rightarrow \overline{k(G/e)^G}$. Rotating the coinduction-restriction adjunction, we obtain $C_e^G \left( \overline{k(G/e)^G} \right) $.

    Now let $k \rightarrow K$ any map with $K$ algebraically closed. Then $K \cong C_e^G \mathbb{F}$ for some algebraically closed field $\mathbb{F}$. Rotating the coinduction-restriction adjunction and applying fixed-points, we obtain a map \[ k(G/e)^G \subset k(G/e) \rightarrow \mathbb{F} \textrm{.} \] Since $k(G/e)$ is integral over $k(G/e)^G$ (by \cite[Exercise 5.12]{AM69}), this map factors through \[ k(G/e) \rightarrow \overline{k(G/e)^G} \rightarrow \mathbb{F} \textrm{,} \] where the first map is our fixed choice of algebraic closure of $k(G/e)^G$. Applying $C_e^G$ to the second map yields a morphism of Nullstellensatzian Tambara functors which manifestly factors $k \rightarrow K$ on the $G/e$ level. Since all objects are fields, all restriction maps are injective, so checking that $k \rightarrow C_e^G \overline{k(G/e)^G}$ factors $k \rightarrow K$ may be done on the $G/e$ level.
